new_statements.quote: El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva. [...] [p.56] De acuerdo al informe de la Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, además de registrar el acento fijo (agudo o último) también se registra los patrones de acentuación: acento penúltimo y acento en sílaba pesada, que ocurren en muy pocas palabras y en algunas variantes.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern in all variants of the Kaqchikel language is fixed; its function is demarcative and its position is on the final syllable (acute/last-syllable stress). It is invariant under derivation. Therefore it need not be written, because it is predictable and has no distinctive function. [...] According to the report of the Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, besides fixed (final) stress, the patterns penultimate stress and heavy-syllable stress are also recorded; they occur in very few words and in some variants.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel (Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala); investigadores Juan Esteban Ajsivinac Sián, Lolmay Pedro Oscar García Mátzar, Martín Chacach Cutzal, Ixchel Carmelina Espantzay / I. E. Alonzo Guaján. 2004. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'äl. Chimaltenango, Guatemala: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, ALMG.
new_statements.locator: cap. Fonología, sección 'Acento', printed p.55 (PDF p.59); exceptions p.56 (PDF p.60)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the held page renders (printed p.55, header FONOLOGIA, section 'Acento') and printed p.56) of ALMG/CLK 2004 'Gramatica descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel'. The quoted passage is there verbatim: p.55 'El patron de acentuacion en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su funcion es demarcativa y su posicion es en silaba final (acento agudo o ultimo). Es invariable en el proceso de derivacion. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce funcion distintiva.' followed by underlined final-syllable examples (nupatz'an, patan, kumatz, qitzij, poqolaj..) and 'Acento en el sufijo de derivacion (silaba final)'; p.56 'De acuerdo al informe de la Comunida…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the word (root, derived word or compound); derivational suffixes and enclitics carry the stress when added. This holds across all Kaqchikel dialects, including the Sololá-area (Western) towns in the ALMG dialect survey; OKMA 1997 (co-describing San Andrés Semetabaj, Sololá) and Bennett's Sololá corpus study state the same final-stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: ALMG 2004 says nothing about secondary stress. Bennett 2018 (Glossa, fn.7): secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel and there is no phonotactic evidence for it; compounds may carry one (final) stress per prosodic word.
new_statements.exceptions: Penultimate stress in a handful of native words (vakix 'cow', tukur 'owl', tata 'señor', nana 'señora', b'alam 'jaguar', anxa 'garlic', janila 'much') and in Spanish loans that are paroxytone (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma); in most variants vakix/tukur lose the second vowel (wakx, tukr). A 'heavy-syllable stress' pattern in very few transitive verb forms only in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé Milpas Altas and Magdalena Milpas Altas (none of these are Sololá/Western towns). OKMA 1997 p.20-21 adds: enclitics (directionals) on verbs/statives take the stress; loans keep Spanish stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (palabra: radical, derivada o compuesta); stress shifts to derivational suffixes and to enclitics. Bennett 2018: domain of stress = prosodic word; prefixes never stressed. Statement is at Kaqchikel language level with an explicit 'en todas las variantes' claim backed by a dialect survey that includes Sololá, Panajachel, Santa Catarina Palopó, San Antonio Palopó, San Lucas Tolimán and San Marcos La Laguna.
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1279 'Kaqchikel, Western' is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for retired ISO [ckw] (Ethnologue 15: 77,000 speakers, northern and eastern shores of Lake Atitlán, Sololá dept.), merged into Kaqchikel [cak] (kaqc1270) by ISO CR 2008-053 in 2009. No [ckw]-specific description exists; the quoted statement is at Kaqchikel language level (ALMG 2004) but explicitly claims 'todas las variantes' on the basis of a dialect survey that includes the Sololá-area towns. Corroborated for the Western area by OKMA 1997 (García Matzar & Rodríguez Guaján), which describes the authors' own variants Tecpán and San Andrés Semetabaj (Sololá), p.20: 'acento fijo.. agudo.. siempre va a recaer en la sílaba final de la palabra', and by Bennett's Sololá corpus study (stressed syllable 'casi siempre es la última sílaba de la palabra'). A catalog entry should probably be filed under kaqc1270 [cak] with this code as an alias.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2018. Recursive prosodic words in Kaqchikel (Mayan). Glossa 3(1): 67, 1-33. doi:10.5334/gjgl.550
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.11-12: domain of stress is the prosodic word; 'stress is basically restricted to word-final position in Kaqchikel'; prefixes uniformly unstressed; compounds may carry one stress per prosodic word. fn.7: 'Secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel'; lax vowels and [ʔC] clusters occur only in stressed word-final syllables; 'safest to assume that there is no word-level secondary stress at all'.

sources.note: p.55: stress is fixed in ALL variants of Kaqchikel, demarcative, on the final syllable (acento agudo), invariant under derivation, not. p.56: per the CLK dialect-variation report, penultimate stress in very few native words (vakix, tukur, tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila) and in Spanish loans; a 'heavy-syllable' pattern in very few words only in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua, Parramos, San Bartolomé and Magdalena Milpas Altas (not Sololá). Dialect data include Sololá, Panajachel, Santa Catarina Palopó, San Antonio Palopó, San Lucas Tolimán, San Marcos La Laguna.

sources.note: p.xii: grammar describes the authors' own variants Iximche' (Tecpán) and Semetab'aj (San Andrés Semetabaj, Sololá -- inside the Western [ckw] area). p.20: 'El Kaqchikel se caracteriza por tener acento fijo.. El acento es agudo.. siempre va a recaer en la sílaba final de la palabra (radical, derivada o compuesta..)'; enclitics added to verbs/statives attract the stress; no tilde needed. p.21: Spanish loans keep penult/antepenult stress (kaxa, xara, anma); a few native exceptions: nana, tata (initial stress), Comalapa janila, Tecpán b'ala.
